text:
Objective design merits testing before adding text. [gSASRec (2024 extended abstract)](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf) attributes SASRec instability partly to overconfidence from sampled BCE and introduces generalized BCE. [Prakash et al. (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276) compare uniform, popularity, in-batch, mixed and adaptive sampling: effectiveness and popularity bias depend on the dataset; harder or popularity-based negatives are not universally better. Uniform multi-negative sampled softmax is therefore an essential baseline.

Sampling correction needs care. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.09331) shows that conventional logQ derivations mishandle the positive, which is always included rather than sampled. Their correction treats positive and negative contributions differently and introduces an uncertainty-based weight. For false-negative mitigation, [CATS (SIGIR 2026)](https://iris.uniroma1.it/handle/11573/1775773) uses item clusters and Thompson sampling, progressively reducing sampling from the positive’s cluster while exploring neighboring clusters. This offers a useful hypothesis, though cluster proximity does not establish whether an unobserved item is relevant.

Practical experiment proposal: hold SASRec fixed; compare uniform sampled softmax across modest negative counts, gBCE, then a uniform/semi-hard mixture with warm-up. Exclude padding, the target and observed training positives; never use held-out interactions for filtering. Treat corrected nonuniform sampling as a separate ablation, using the actual proposal probabilities—top-k mining changes that distribution. These are experimental recommendations, not established gains on this task. Select by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 and GPU cost; lower loss or wider training margins cannot establish improvement against the fixed 99-negative candidates.
